summary: Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (Dr. phil., ~1949–1955) and Ludwig Alsdorf (Habilitation, ~1955–1964). He served as professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin from ~1966 to 1994.

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Munich under Friedrich Wilhelm. He held teaching posts at Munich, the Free University of Berlin, and Humboldt University before serving as chairholder at Tübingen (1999–2017).

Klaus Fischer was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (~1945–1948) and studied under J. N. Banerjea and O. C. Gangoly in 1952. He was a professor at the University of Bonn (1966–1985).

Klaus Hahlweg worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetan studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Helmuth von Glasenapp and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Munich in 1954 under Helmut Hoffmann.

Klaus Karttunen is an Indologist, linguist, and historian who earned his BA at the University of Helsinki (1971–1974), studying under Pentti Aalto and Asko Parpola. He held research and teaching posts at the Academy of Finland and the University of Helsinki.

Klaus Ludwig Janert was an Indologist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Frankfurt, Göttingen under Paul Thieme (PhD 1954), and Tübingen (Habilitation 1962). He worked at Göttingen, lectured at Tübingen (1962–1963), and was professor of Indology at Cologne (1963–1987).

Klaus Matzel was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the Free University of Berlin (~1951–1956) and his habilitation at Würzburg (~1963–1968). He taught at Peradeniya (~1958–1962) and served as professor of Germanic philology at Regensburg (1968–1989).

Klaus Mylius was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Weller and Karl Ammer, earning degrees at Halle-Wittenberg and Leipzig. He was a lecturer at Leipzig (1970–1991), Bayreuth (1990–1994), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1996–2022).
Klaus Pinte is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and sinology. He studied at Ghent University under Pol Vanden Broucke and served as postdoctoral teaching staff there in 2006.

Klaus Röhrborn is a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leipzig, Hamburg, and Giessen under Bertold Spuler, Wolfgang Lentz, and Annemarie von Gabain. He was a professor at Giessen (1972) and Göttingen (1992–2003).

Klaus Rüping is an Indologist who studied at the University of Bonn under Paul Hacker and completed his PhD at the University of Münster (1968). He spent his academic career at Münster, becoming an ordinary professor in 1980.

Klaus Strunk was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Karl Hoffmann (~1954–1961). He held professorial posts at Saarland University (~1968–1977) and the University of Munich (~1977–1998).

Klaus Wille is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He worked on manuscript cataloging for the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 1997) and held research posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2000–2009 and 2018–2026).

Klaus-Dieter Mathes specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bonn, Marburg under Michael Hahn, and Hamburg. He served as a researcher at Hamburg, professor at the University of Vienna (2010), and professor of Buddhist studies at the University of Hong Kong (2023).

Klaus-Josef Notz was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at PTH Benediktbeuern (1966–1971) and completed a Doctor theologiae at the University of Munich (1978–1984), where he served as a lecturer in 1996.
Klemens Karlsson is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who completed his Doctor of Philosophy at Uppsala University in 2000 under the supervision of Peter Schalk.

Knut A. Jacobsen is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1989–1994). He was appointed professor at the University of Bergen in 1996 and was attested at the University of Oslo in 1999.

Knut Kristiansen was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the University of Oslo under Georg Morgenstierne. He served as a university lecturer in Modern Indic languages at the University of Oslo from 1971 to 1998.

Kobun Otogawa was a Buddhist studies teacher who studied at Komazawa University, Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, and Eihei-ji. He held teaching posts at Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967–1970), Haiku Zendo (1970–1978), and Naropa University (2001).

Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Keido Ito, Gen'ei Kato, and Bokusan Nishiari. He held multiple leadership posts at Komazawa University between 1892 and 1909 and lectured at the University of Tokyo.
